The final M3GNet interatomic potential achieves test mean absolute errors of 0.035 eV/atom for energy, 0.072 eV/Å for forces, and 0.41 GPa for stresses on a held‑out Materials Project dataset covering 89 elements.

evidence.text: Machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on OMat24 predict tightly converged DFT forces with accuracy comparable to or better than predictions for less tightly converged calculations.

evidence.text: M3GNet predicts phonon band structures and densities of states for SiO₂ polymorphs that quantitatively agree with DFT calculations, and the predicted phonon density‑of‑states center follows the expected ω ∝ 1/√m trend across materials.

A graph convolutional neural network predicts vibrational free energies with root‑mean‑square errors of 8.23 meV/atom (training), 11.34 meV/atom (validation) and 12.31 meV/atom (test), and its predictions for MgS and NaH polymorphs match DFT‑computed values across the 200–700 K range.
For monolayer MoS₂, DeepH predicts DFT Hamiltonian matrix elements with average mean absolute errors of 1.3 meV (Mo–Mo), 1.0 meV (Mo–S), 0.7 meV (S–Mo), and 0.8 meV (S–S).

source_span.text: universal MLIPs show inaccuracies despite good energy/force performance

evidence.text: U-MLIPs systematically underpredict energies and forces due to softening of the potential energy surface, attributed to biased sampling in training datasets from DFT ionic relaxations near local PES minima.

DFT setting inconsistency between training and evaluation datasets significantly affects MLIP model performance comparisons, with PET-OMAD performing worse than PET-OAM and PET-MPtrj on Inorganic Materials due to differences in ab initio theory levels.

Metal-organic frameworks present an ideal application for MLIPs because classical force fields lack required accuracy while DFT is too computationally expensive for large unit cells and long timescales.

The k-MVN method can predict full phonon band structures at arbitrary k points in the Brillouin zone by incorporating momentum dependence through phase factors for unit-cell translations.

source_span.text: universal MLIPs show inaccuracies despite good energy/force performance

evidence.text: Foundational MLIP models often fail to outperform simple classical force fields for MOF systems without long-range corrections.

Non-conservative (unconstrained) MLIP models consistently show 2-3× theoretical speed-up over their conservative counterparts, with direct force prediction providing additional 2-3× speedup compared to forces computed via automatic differentiation.

Elastic moduli predictions are very sensitive to the lack of energy conservation in MLIP models, and non-conservative models consistently perform worse on matbench-discovery downstream tasks despite achieving better training and validation accuracies.

source_span.text: phonon property prediction

evidence.text: MACE‑MP‑0 attains state‑of‑the‑art accuracy for periodic systems while preserving equivariant inductive biases.
MACE-MP0 emerged as the best model for vibrational properties, while ALIGNN-FF demonstrated significant qualitative errors in reproducing phonon band structures.

The computational cost of MACE scales O(1) with the number of chemical elements because species embeddings are continuous and not included in the tensor‑product contraction, and higher‑order features are implemented via an efficient single‑loop tensor‑contraction algorithm.

source_span.text: universal MLIPs show inaccuracies despite good energy/force performance

evidence.text: None of the three U-MLIPs (M3GNet, CHGNet, MACE-MP0) could accurately reproduce mixing energies of metallic binary alloys in adequate agreement with DFT results.
MACE‑MP‑0 attains state‑of‑the‑art accuracy for periodic systems while preserving equivariant inductive biases.

MACE evaluates roughly ten times faster than prior force‑field models for invariant (L=0) architectures and 4–5 times faster for equivariant (L=1,2) architectures, while delivering lower prediction errors.
